messages.author: fd0699def5740093
messages.subject: heteroskedasticity
parts:
Hi,

I have been trying to work out how to fit the following model in INLA

Cover: response (percent cover ranging from 0 to 1)
Year: categorical predictor with 32 levels - ideally needs to be categoical for numerous reasons.
REEF_NAME: 'random effect' - approx 50 to 100 levels depending on the data location

BRMS
---------------
mod_brms.beta.disp <- brm(bf(Cover ~ Year + (1|REEF_NAME), phi~0+Year),
                                       data=dat,
                                       family=Beta(link='logit'),
                                       iter=1e4, warmup=5e3, thin=5,
                                       chains=4, cores=4,
                                       prior = prior(normal(0, 3), class = "b") +
                                           prior(normal(0, 3), class = "Intercept") +
                                           prior(gamma(2, 1), class = "sd") 
                                       )

glmmTMB
--------------------
mod_glmmTMB.beta.disp <- glmmTMB(Cover ~ Year + (1|REEF_NAME),
                                     dispformula = ~Year,
                                     data=dat,
                                     family=beta_family())

Whilst these two models run find, the stan model in particular takes about 11 hours to run.

The following INLA model runs in about 30 seconds and yields results indistinguishable from brms (without phii ~..) and glmmTMB (without disp ~ ..):
mod_inla.beta <-inla(Cover~Year + f(REEF_NAME, model='iid'), 
                                                    dat=dat,
                                                    family='beta',
                                                    control.fixed=list(mean=0, prec=0.001, 
                                                    mean.intercept=0.5, prec.intercept=0.001)
)


Kind regards and thanks in advance

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] heteroskedasticity
parts:
Hi Murray,

you didn't define the heteroscedasticity in the text, so it took me a while to realise that the brms and glmmmTB code has some extra features.
It looks like you want the variance of the REEF_NAME variables to be different for each Year?

From what I can tell in your model construction, that means that you could just estimate a completely separate model for each year, since there's nothing to link them together.
Unless you want another hierarchical layer for the variances? I don't believe that's possible in the R-INLA implementation, since it doesn't follow the theta->latent->observed hierarchical structure.

However, this extra structure can in principle be approximated using a non-linear predictor in the inlabru package. By parameterising the variances as transformations of N(0,1) variables, one can construct a non-linear model via

  comp <- ~ Year + REEF(REEF_NAME, model = "iid") + scale(Year, model = "iid", hyper = list(prec=list(initial=0,fixed=TRUE)), constr=TRUE)
  formula <- Cover ~ Year + REEF * scalequantile(pnorm(scale))
  bru(comp, like(data=dat, formula=formula, family="beta"), options=list(control.inla=..., ...))

where scalequantile() is the quantile function for the desired prior for the scaling parameters. The resulting variances would be determined by the combination of a precision hyperparameter for the REEF random effects and the Year-wise scaling parameters. The sum-to-zero constraint is to ensure identifiability, but there are other options, such as fixing the precision of REEF instead, in which scalequantile() would directly determine the standard deviation priors, but that would then be indistinguishable from estimating separate models for each Year.  The suggestion above will estimate a common precision parameter, and the scale parameters model the deviation from that overall precision.

If you use this approach, please contact me off list as well, as I'm not aware of this feature being used for this particular purpose yet.

PS. "scalequantile(pnorm())" should ideally be implemented as a single function that used log.p=TRUE and lower.tail=TRUE/FALSE intelligently to preserve as much numerical precision as possible. I'm planning an automated feature for that in the package soon(ish) as we're finding more and more uses for this technique.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] heteroskedasticity
parts:
comp <- ~ Year + REEF(REEF_NAME, model = "iid") + scale(Year, model = "iid", hyper = list(prec=list(initial=0,fixed=TRUE)), constr=TRUE)
  formula <- Cover ~ Year + REEF * scalequantile(pnorm(scale))

I forgot to include a parameter option for the scale model:
  comp <- ~ Year + REEF(REEF_NAME, model = "iid") + scale(Year, model = "iid", hyper = list(prec=list(initial=0,fixed=TRUE)), constr=TRUE) + param(1)
  formula <- Cover ~ Year + REEF * scalequantile(pnorm(scale), param) 
That allows us to e.g. estimate a precision parameter for the scale parameter distribution itself (i.e. another hierarchical layer of the model).

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] heteroskedasticity
parts: But to be clear: if phi is the variance (or precision), then “having them drawn from the same prior” in a pure sense decouples the years completely and you can just run one model for each year. You only need to estimate them jointly if you’re also estimating any parameters in he distribution for phi. Drawing a DAG and spelling out the actual model structure as conditional distribution will help clarify exactly what the model is intended to be.

Finn

its possible to allow for a linear model for the log precision for the
beta. some, or rather, a few, likelihood models have that option, but
not yet for family=beta. its about one day of work...

if you know the scaling of the precisions there is the argument 'scale',
but this what you want to estimate, not set.

>   comp <- ~ Year + REEF(REEF_NAME, model = "iid") + scale(Year, model
> = "iid", hyper = list(prec=list(initial=0,fixed=TRUE)), constr=TRUE)
>   formula <- Cover ~ Year + REEF * scalequantile(pnorm(scale))
>   bru(comp, like(data=dat, formula=formula, family="beta"),
> options=list(control.inla=..., ...))
>
> where scalequantile() is the quantile function for the desired prior
> for the scaling parameters. The resulting variances would be
> determined by the combination of a precision hyperparameter for the
> REEF random effects and the Year-wise scaling parameters. The sum-to-
> zero constraint is to ensure identifiability, but there are other
> options, such as fixing the precision of REEF instead, in which
> scalequantile() would directly determine the standard deviation
> priors, but that would then be indistinguishable from estimating
> separate models for each Year.  The suggestion above will estimate a
> common precision parameter, and the scale parameters model the
> deviation from that overall precision.
>
> If you use this approach, please contact me off list as well, as I'm
> not aware of this feature being used for this particular purpose yet.
>
> PS. "scalequantile(pnorm())" should ideally be implemented as a single
> function that used log.p=TRUE and lower.tail=TRUE/FALSE intelligently
> to preserve as much numerical precision as possible. I'm planning an
> automated feature for that in the package soon(ish) as we're finding
> more and more uses for this technique.
